experiment: Semantic Film Director 2.0 (claim logic + shot reads + visual proof + camera purpose) — pre-registered blind A / B / C (preregistration-c12.json): A = shipped storyboard, B = Director 1.0 (C11), C = Director 2.0
raters: AGENT raters only: 119 fresh sonnet describers (one strip each, image only), 2 x 30 fresh sonnet judges (up to 4 descriptions of 4 different beats each, frozen answer key + narration). No human rating was collected — human reference prepared for three arms, NOT run.

plus20.value: C - A = +8.3 pp (A 30.6 % -> C 38.9 %), paired bootstrap 95 % CI 0 ... +17.5

wrongNotUp.value: WRONG frames A 3 -> C 4.5 (mean of two judge passes, 90 frames per arm)

regressionWithin10.value: regression set C - A +8.3 pp (n 10, CI -15 ... +36.7)

componentsAddValue.value: C - B = -8.3 pp (B 47.2 % -> C 38.9 %), CI -20.3 ... +1.7; pre-registered rule needed diff > 0 and CI lower bound > -5

ablations: NOT RUN — pre-registered trigger (SHIP and C - B >= +10 pp) not met
BvsA_replication: B - A = +16.7 pp on this fresh holdout (A 30.6 % -> B 47.2 %); C11 measured +5.3 pp on its own set. Exploratory: B was not the arm under test.

claimPolarity.polarityErrors_main: A 2, B 0, C 0 (beats whose key lists notAsserted parts: n 18)
claimPolarity.regressionTests: scripts/test-semantic-director-v2.js — 13 / 13 pass, incl. dev-set B05 (rejected premise must not become the quote card) and B17 (setup half of a contrast drawn as negated)
claimPolarity.note: C removed polarity errors, but so did B on this set; the claim-logic layer is not what separated the arms.

subgroups_exploratory.note: not decision criteria; n is small — read as direction, not proof
subgroups_exploratory.textOnlyUse: B chose a quote card (H) on 11 of 30 main beats, C on 1 (the recorded-reason rule worked as intended)
subgroups_exploratory.BtextOnly_Cpicture_n10: A 34.2 / B 44.2 / C 39.2 — replacing B's quote cards with C's pictures lost ~5 pp
subgroups_exploratory.bothPicture_n19: A 27.6 / B 46.0 / C 35.5 — C's picture lost ~10 pp to B's picture on the same beats

findings: Director 2.0 makes pictures carry more (ADDS 32 -> 65 vs A, 43 -> 65 vs B) but the muted viewer understood LESS than with Director 1.0: comprehension C 38.9 % vs B 47.2 %. Busier frames that each say something are not the same as a clearer point.

The loss is not only the quote-card swap: on the 19 beats where both B and C drew a picture, C still lost ~10 pp. The progressive build split the proof into timed reads (entities per staged beat barely changed: B 2.6, C 2.8) and the viewer read the parts, not the relation (C30: three elements seen, the setup -> payoff link missed; C16: only the first half of the reward schedule).
Dropping text-only from 11 to 1 beat removed B's best scorers where the sentence IS the point (C01, C23, C34): the recorded-reason rule was too strict for beats whose meaning is verbal.
Claim logic did its narrow job (0 polarity errors, B05 / B17 regressions pass) but polarity was not the bottleneck on this holdout (A made 2 errors, B 0).
WRONG rose A 3 -> C 4.5: new verbs (cover / reveal) and staged objects were read literally (C24: a planned stink-bomb read as an actual car crash).
Director 1.0 replicated better than in C11 (+16.7 pp vs A on a fresh holdout, CI not computed against the +20 bar for B); it remains the stronger of the two research directors.

authoringBias.B: fresh sonnet authors from the C11 spec, one pass + one compile-fix pass; 40 / 40 compile
authoringBias.C: fresh sonnet authors from director-spec-v2.md, one pass + one compile-fix pass; 39 / 40 compile (C29 reads 1.48 s < 1.5 s minimum = arm C failure, scored 0)
authoringBias.A: the shipped storyboard: authored, gated, multi-round fixed per book — more effort than B or C
authoringBias.direction: B and C had the same authoring budget; the experimenter wrote both specs and the renderers, not the contracts; authors were blind to the key and the rating

deviations: deviations.json (2, both before any benchmark render or rating: v2 cover read-target validator fix; v2 before-state / outline / reveal-line render fix) + ratings/repairs.log (one describer JSON missing a ']' — syntax only).

humanReference.materials: human-reference.md, human-sheet-c12.js (30 scenes x 3 strips, X / Y / Z order by seeded permutation), answer-key.json, rating-prompts.md
humanReference.estimatedCost: ≈ 11 h rater time (5 raters) + ≈ 5 h scoring (2 scorers)

subjectMotionCheck: report-only design in cinecode-audit.md §3 (camera-motion-subtracted residual); not built — still-based verdicts cannot see motion, so it cannot move this metric
animaticFeasibility: cinecode-audit.md §2: feasible with existing Remotion (frame range at --scale=0.33, low CRF, on the cloud stills runner); ~1/9 the pixels of a full render; nothing to port. Not built in C12 because the rating is still-based.

costAndScale.authoring: same order as C11: ≈ 8 k sonnet tokens per beat (spec as input); v2 spec is longer (claim + reads) — ≈ 1.3x per beat
costAndScale.render: SemanticStage2 is plain SVG; 119 strips / 357 stills on 12 cloud runners in 159 s wall (run 41980783311); 0 local renders
costAndScale.rating: 119 describers + 60 judges ≈ 9.6 M sonnet tokens (session limit hit once; resumed)
costAndScale.fullBookImpact: opt-in scene field (semantic.v === 2); old configs draw unchanged; production integration NOT done (NO SHIP)
